The bank why shouts COMBINED in capitals, and its trap note on 2 hr ("used 200/100 instead of 200/80") names no reason; the explainer calls it a slip with no clean route.

routing: Needs a route: the view opens from data-go="rate-time"; its rate sliders need a state reader. The skill page opens with a Try first question on a 5-minute clock that can be skipped, and the page also holds a timed simulator elsewhere; the visual itself is untimed.

served.stem: Two cars start 200 miles apart, driving toward each other. One at 50 mph, the other 30 mph. When do they meet?
served.bankWhy: They close the gap at COMBINED speed: 50 + 30 = 80 mph. Time = 200 / 80 = 2.5 hours.

answer.line: The gap closes 50 + 30 = 80 miles every hour, so 200 miles takes 200 / 80 = 2.5 hours.

steps: Follow the gap, not one car. Driving toward each other, both cars eat into it, so the speeds add: 80 mph.
Time to meet is the gap over the closing speed: 200 / 80 = 2.5 hours.
Check it: in 2.5 hours one car drives 125 miles and the other 75. 125 + 75 = 200.

choices.note: 5 hours uses 40 mph, the average of the two speeds. Toward each other, the speeds add: 80 mph.
200 / 30 is the slower car closing the whole gap alone, as if the other were parked. Both are moving.
No single slip lands on 2 hours: that needs a closing speed of 100. The speeds add to 80.
200 / 50 is the faster car covering the whole gap alone. The other car closes 30 miles of it every hour too.

student.lockIt: Moving toward each other, the speeds add. Time to meet is the gap over the closing speed.
